# Colophon {.unnumbered}

This book was produced with [Quarto](https://quarto.org).
Its examples use R, the `zzcollab` framework, Docker, and
`renv`, each introduced in the chapter that first requires
it.

Fittingly for its subject, the book is built as a Quarto
project: the sources render to HTML and PDF with `quarto
render`, and wherever the book presents a computed figure
or table, that result is generated at build time from the
code shown beside it, so the printed output and the code
that produced it cannot drift apart. The table below is
itself an instance of that discipline: every cell is read
from the actual session that rendered this copy of the
book, not typed by hand, so it cannot silently fall out of
step with the build that produced it.


::: {#tbl-colophon .cell tbl-cap='The actual rendering environment for this build, read from the live session rather than recorded by hand.'}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Field              |Value                        |
|:------------------|:----------------------------|
|R version          |R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24) |
|Platform           |aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0   |
|Quarto version     |not reported by renderer     |
|Package: tibble    |3.3.1                        |
|Package: ggplot2   |4.0.3                        |
|Package: withr     |3.0.3                        |
|Package: knitr     |1.51                         |
|Package: rmarkdown |2.31                         |
|renv.lock present  |no                           |


:::
:::


The last row is the book's own honest reproducibility
disclosure, made the same way the book asks every analysis
to make it: by naming the artifact rather than asserting
the level. As of this build there is no `renv.lock` for the
book's own source, so the table above reports `no`; pinning
the book's own environment to the L1 and L2 standard the
later chapters teach is planned, not yet complete, and this
colophon will report `yes` automatically, with no prose
change required, the day that lockfile exists.

Last rendered: see the build timestamp on the homepage.
